title: Open a flat shopping tote, pack two groceries and lift it by both handles
instruction: Put the box of crackers and the pack of toilet rolls into the bag so that both rest on the bag's base and the bag stands upright on its own. Then lift the bag by its two handles, set it back down, let go and move both arms away.
context: At a grocery checkout a reusable tote can arrive folded flat. Open its walls, pack the small carton and the bulky bundle, and lift the loaded bag by both handles. O*NET lists bagging merchandise among cashier duties (41-2011.00). Unlike simulated bag-insertion benchmarks such as DeformableRavens bag-items, where small blocks drop into an already-open sack, the robot must first stand up a collapsed tote whose walls fall back unless held, then insert a pack wider than one gripper with both hands while keeping the walls up, and finally lift the loaded bag by both handles without it tipping or spilling.
setup:
All dimensions in mm. The origin is on the tabletop at the middle of the line through the arm bases. x points forward, y to the robot's left, z up. On a wooden 1100 x 1300 tabletop, two YAM arms with parallel grippers (pads 94 apart when open) start at ready, bases at (0, +305) and (0, -305), grippers open. One overhead camera and one camera on each wrist.
1) Build the green tote to docs/tote-pattern.svg and the README assembly instructions. Target empty mass 109 g. A 310 x 160 corrugated polypropylene base board lies long side along x inside an 80 g/m² non-woven polypropylene shell. Straightened rim height above the tabletop is 180. Each wall has one light horizontal crease at 90. The two large walls fold inward, the ends outward. Centred on each large wall's top edge is a cream stiffened webbing loop, 150 outside width x 90 from rim to far grip edge, padded grip 18 wide x 10 thick. Fabric hinges let the loops swing outward. A stop at each root keeps the grip outside the mouth. Centre the board on (360, 70). Fold both ends outward, then the right and left large walls inward, doubling each wall back at its crease. The simulated folded body covers x 119 to 601, y -9 to 149 and is 26 high. Lay the handles outside that footprint, grip centres at (360, 227) and (360, -85).
2) Cracker-box stand-in. A closed red paperboard carton, 60 x 132 x 215 high, packed to 280 g, stands centred on (220, 245) with the 132 side along y. One gripper can hold the 60 side.
3) Four-roll stand-in. Four paper rolls wrapped in film, two across x and two high, roll axes along y. Finished pack 200 x 100 x 200 high, 360 g, white with blue-green markings. Stand it centred on (405, -170) with the 200 long side along x. Its narrowest side exceeds the gripper opening. Both groceries stand taller than the rim and fit side by side on the board.
After building and before each physical session, run the README acceptance check on the actual tote and both stand-ins. Record dimensions and masses (each within 10 g of target), released folded height on the marks (at most 30), and loaded height (all four wall tops at least 144 for 10 s hands-free). Each handle must stay outside the mouth line under 2 N inward at the grip. Remove measuring tools and reset all three objects to their marks for the trial.
In the overhead policy image (320 x 176) the collapsed bag's base board is about 48 x 29 pixels, the box's top 13 x 31, the pack's top 33 x 21, and each handle grip a light bar 23 x 3 on the table. The wrist cameras see them larger once a gripper is near.
scoring: Scored on the state at the end of the trial (the run limit, or as soon as the 1.0 state has lasted 2 seconds). Nothing is scored for the order in which the items go in or for how they are held. Definitions. An item rests on the base: its lowest point is within 3 mm of the bag's base board, it stands on one of its faces (that face within 10 degrees of the board) and, seen from above, it lies wholly within the board's outline; an item lying on a folded-in wall is higher than that and does not count. The bag stands upright: its base board is on the table (lowest point within 5 mm of it), level within 10 degrees, its middle within 50 mm of its tape marks, and the top edge of each of its four walls is at least 144 mm above the table (80 % of 180). The lift is done once, for 2 seconds without a break, the base board's lowest point is at least 50 mm above the table, both handle grips are pulled at least 30 mm above the bag's top edge and both items remain in the bag. In the lift, each item’s centre stays over the base outline and its lower edge stays below the top of the bag. Check that neither exits on the video. Check the 3 mm base gap only after set-down. 1.0: both items rest on the base, the bag stands upright, the lift is done, and for the last 2 seconds no part of the robot touches the bag or an item and both grippers' centre points are at least 50 mm from the bag (its outline up to its top edge, and its handle grips). 0.75: both items rest on the base and the bag stands upright, but the lift is not done or the robot has not let go. 0.5: the pack of toilet rolls rests on the base and the bag stands upright (the box is anywhere). 0.25: only the box of crackers rests on the base and the bag stands upright. 0: anything else, including a bag that at the end is held up, lying over, slumped or more than 50 mm off its marks. Also 0, whatever happens later, once an item has fallen off the worktable, an item has come out of the bag while the bag was off the table, or a corner seam of the bag has been pulled more than 30 mm apart (torn). On a real trial: film from the side; at the end hold a ruler against each wall, photograph the bag from above and from the side, and try a 3 mm card under each item inside the bag. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Take both items out of the bag. Fold the bag down on its tape marks (base board centred on (360, 70)): the two end walls outward flat on the table, then the right large wall and then the left one inward flat on the base board, and lay each handle flat on the table beside the bag. Stand the box on its marks, centred on (220, 245), and the pack on its marks, centred on (405, -170). Return both arms to ready with grippers open. Replace a bag with a torn seam or handle, a crushed box and a burst pack. In simulation: seed 0, zero object jitter; the bag's joints, both items and the scorer are returned to their start state.
fidelity: The simulated tote follows the construction dimensions and mass target. Wall and crease stiffness and contact friction are estimates without measurements on a built bag. PhysX runs at 240 Hz with 20 Hz control. Two rigid panels per wall approximate fabric folds. Colliders are 2 mm thick at the walls, 4 mm at the board. Panel masses are raised. Elastic corner ties have a 30 mm tear proxy. Rigid handle hinges allow 10° inward travel. Both groceries are rigid.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 in 2400 steps; scripted: 1.0 in 1620. Both recorded with the current files and grader.
